what: one-window decision test of the runner-up: batching the small GEMV calls
premise_correction: z/rec/ab are stamps INSIDE the fused GDN kernel, not separate launches; the only separate small GEMVs are the shared expert's gate/up/down and the k/v projections, so the batch target is the shared block (~3 calls/layer), not five

measurements.window_run: 1K/256 one-shot on the reverted binary: 114.04 tok/s (trajectory band); the one-shot does not print the serve-path stage lines, so in-situ numbers are from r31f

analysis: the shared block's three calls cost ~26 us/layer at T=3.17 (~1.24 ms/window), matching the 1.57 ms shared+quant stage; a 3-job single launch could save the launch/teardown plus some occupancy fill, bounded by ~0.4-0.5 ms/window (1.2-1.5% of the 35 ms round) because the weights (1.74 MB each) must be read regardless and the shapes are latency-bound at 23-39% of the wall
verdict: NOT WORTH BUILDING: the bound (1.2-1.5%) sits below the pre-declared >=2% gate, and the kernel risk (three forms/act images, per-job shape) is high for that. The runner-up is closed; no code change.
caveat: the bench uses synthetic Q8_0 at the engine's shapes; the engine stores the HC weights bf16 (6.55 MB per matrix) and the shared tensors at their own quant types, so these are shape/pattern bounds, not exact engine bytes
